name: manual_ff093a
claim: Before global heartbeat cleanup, stop affected workers, automatic restarts and queue mutations, and keep them quiesced until cleanup finishes; recheck the complete affected set under that maintenance window. If continuing quiescence cannot be established, do not run cleanup: the current implementation does not atomically recheck liveness before releasing each claim, so a restarting worker can lose its claim. Heartbeat cleanup now handles both legacy and queue claims for all agents classified DEAD, so verify liveness and independently inspect every affected claim before operator-authorized global cleanup; stale heartbeat alone does not prove death. Cleanup requeues queue claims even at the retry limit: hold exhausted or unsafe work and seek separately reviewed authorized recovery. An agent release event alone does not clear a queue claim. Queue completion requires queue complete <task_id> <claimant_id> --expected-claimed-at <claimed_at> and checks both the current claimant and that claim's timestamp; never impersonate an absent claimant. Verify completion artifacts independently, and remember a reserved handoff retains required_agent_id after requeue. Pass the claimed_at printed by your own queue claim. --unverified-legacy skips that fence: use it only when your own stamp is lost, never for a takeover. A takeover is disclosed under the author-actor takeover policy and is not impersonation (the original claimant stays the author, you are the actor). It stays fenced: before checking evidence, read the stalled claim's claimed_at once, as PHASE_TRACKING.md section 'Taking over a claimed task' shows; before completing, publish as yourself the prior agent and its status, the immutable work reference, the evidence you checked, that claimed_at and the operation you intend, with any authorization it requires; then run queue complete <task_id> <original_claimant_agent_id> --expected-claimed-at <claimed_at> and repeat the actor and evidence in --notes. If there is no claim row, another agent holds the claim, the claim is newer than the stall you verified, or the completion is refused, do not read the value again or drop the fence: leave the claim held, report the work as unverified and stop. The fence refuses a replacement made after your read, not one made before it. Do not use queue fail for a takeover, because it records activity for the claimant.

decisions.notes: Supersedes lesson_559e29e3ef1e. --unverified-legacy matches only the claimant id, so a takeover that used it could complete a newer claim made under the same name. The claim row always carries claimed_at, so a takeover can read it once and keep the release fence, which compares and releases in one transaction (PR 525 review comment 4721776895). The earlier safety and recovery guidance is carried forward unchanged.
